issues.body: crate_labels_to_provision treats any normalized changed path exactly equal to crates/<name>/Cargo.toml as positive evidence. The path list loses change status and includes previous_filename for renames, so a deleted manifest or the old side of a rename can qualify. Even an added file with that name need not be a valid Cargo manifest. This contradicts the load-bearing claim that the PR establishes a crate and permits durable area-label creation for a crate that does not exist on the resulting PR head. The current tests cover nested and stray paths but not deletion/rename-away or manifest validity.
issues.fix_hint: Carry file status through the changed-file model and accept only added/renamed-to crate-root manifests, then validate the PR-head manifest (at minimum parse it and confirm a package/workspace crate identity consistent with the directory) using a read-only, data-only fetch rather than executing PR code. Add real-path tests proving deletion and previous_filename cannot provision, malformed manifests cannot provision, and a valid added manifest still can.
issues.title: A Cargo.toml path is not sufficient evidence that the PR establishes a crate

verdict.summary: The provisioning path is mostly fail-closed and its effect tests exercise the real write sequence, but the claimed crate evidence is not actually established by the available input. A changed path named crates/<name>/Cargo.toml can represent deletion or rename-away and says nothing about whether the manifest is valid. The code nevertheless turns that path into permanent repository state. Round 2 reported no findings, so this newly identified major correctness/security-boundary issue makes round 3 regressing.
